name: Jaipur
description: Jaipur is the walled Pink City and capital of Rajasthan, built in 1727 to a grid plan unusual for its era. It suits heritage lovers, photographers, and shoppers well, though crowds and aggressive touts at major monuments can be draining. Heat from April through June is severe; October to March is the comfortable window.

attractions.name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort)
attractions.description: A sprawling 16th-century Rajput hilltop fort with elaborate mirror-work interiors, sheesh mahal, and tiered courtyards. The elephant-ride option at the base is controversial for animal-welfare reasons; the uphill jeep or on-foot route is the better choice.

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.description: The former royal seat at the heart of the old walled city, still partly inhabited by the Jaipur royal family. The museum holds royal costumes, arms, and the famous silver water urns, but entry costs have risen steeply and the premium Priveé tour is pricey.

attractions.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
attractions.description: Jaipur's most iconic facade — a five-storey pink sandstone screen built in 1799 so royal women could watch street processions unseen. The interior is modest; most people photograph it from the tea-stall rooftop across Badi Chaupar road.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.description: A UNESCO-listed 18th-century astronomical observatory with 19 massive masonry instruments built by Maharaja Jai Singh II. The Samrat Yantra sundial is the world's largest; a good guide makes the science legible, otherwise it is easy to miss the point.

attractions.name: Nahargarh Fort
attractions.description: A hillside fort on the Aravalli ridge above the city, offering arguably the best panoramic views of Jaipur. Less crowded than Amber, with a rooftop cafe. The road up is narrow and shared with tuk-tuks; auto-rickshaws or private cars are easier than walking.

attractions.name: Jaigarh Fort
attractions.description: A military fort connected to Amber by a covered passage, housing the world's largest wheeled cannon (Jaivana). Less visited than Amber, with good views over the Aravalli hills, but the interior is sparse and best paired with an Amber visit on the same ticket.

attractions.name: Albert Hall Museum (Central Museum)
attractions.description: Rajasthan's oldest museum, housed in an 1887 Indo-Saracenic building with collections of arms, textiles, natural history, and a genuine Egyptian mummy. A good indoor retreat on a hot afternoon; often skipped by hurried tourists to their loss.

attractions.name: Galta Ji (Monkey Temple)
attractions.description: A series of natural spring-fed kund (tank) temples carved into a rocky gorge east of the city, home to hundreds of rhesus macaques. Genuinely atmospheric and far less polished than the main forts; pilgrims bathe in the tanks at dawn. Hold bags tightly — the monkeys steal.

attractions.name: Panna Meena Ka Kund
attractions.description: A 16th-century stepwell near Amber Fort with a symmetrical grid of criss-crossing staircases descending to a central well. It is a hidden gem that most Amber visitors walk past; almost always quiet, visually striking, and free to enter.

attractions.name: Johri Bazaar
attractions.description: The main jewellery and gem market of the old city, one of India's most reputable places to buy Rajasthani silver, kundan, and meenakari work. Bargaining is expected; be wary of gemstone sellers promising investment-grade stones to foreigners.
